messages:
Neyra (AcmeApps): Hey team — we started seeing a bunch of requests from our EU customers with 200+ms additional latency. Console shows the region as eu-west-1 for the route, but our request logs show serving_region=us-central and latency spikes. Happening since ~11:20 UTC. Example request id: req_01FJX9Z4.

Jamie (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste a raw request id (the full one) and a snippet of the server log you saw? Also which API endpoint (generation/embeddings)?

Neyra (AcmeApps): Attached snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T11:22:13Z INFO request=req_01FJX9Z4 route=/v1/generate user=acmeapp serving_region=us-central latency_ms=224 status=200
```
This is for /v1/generate, a short text completion. Console route settings show region badge "eu-west-1" on the dashboard.

Jamie (Support): Thanks — confirmed. Quick question: are you using any region override header or query param? e.g., x-redwood-region or ?region= ?

Neyra (AcmeApps): No explicit override. We relied on the dashboard default region. We have many clients in EU, so we expect eu-west.

Sam (eng-routing): Looping in routing. Short summary: if the configured/primary region is unavailable or at capacity, the routing policy can fail over to a compatible region (we prefer same continent but sometimes US pool is used). That should show up in request traces. Console UI should reflect the final serving region though — that sounds like a display mismatch.

Rachel (eng-console): I dug into the console mapping service — we populate the region badge from the account->preferred_region mapping cached in the console service (TTL 12h). When a fallback occurs at the request layer it doesn't currently invalidate that badge. So the dashboard can show "eu-west-1" while actual requests are routed elsewhere. This is a UI/data inconsistency, not a routing misdecision by the runtime.

Jamie (Support): Thanks Rachel & Sam. Neyra — short-term mitigation: you can pin requests to a region by adding the header `x-redwood-region: eu-west-1` or using `?region=eu-west-1` on the request URL. That forces routing and will return 503 if the region is unavailable (instead of silently failing over). Would you like us to try a pinned request to confirm behavior?

Neyra (AcmeApps): Yes please — send the curl we should run. We can test from our EU client.

Jamie (Support): Try: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate?region=eu-west-1 \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello","max_tokens":10}'
```
If it returns 503 the EU pool is failing over; if it returns 200 it means pinning succeeded. Also include the request-id header from the response for our diagnostics.

Sam (eng-routing): Also adding: routing fallbacks are logged in the request trace: key `fallback_reason` (e.g., cap_exceeded, healthcheck_fail). If you paste that from a failing trace we can confirm cause.

Neyra (AcmeApps): Ran the pinned curl — response 503 w/ body `{ "error": "region unavailable" }` and response header `x-request-id: req_01FJX9Z4`. So looks like EU pool returned unavailable and runtime chose to fail open to us-central for non-pinned requests.

Jamie (Support): Got it — escalating to engineering for console badge fix + routing visibility. Creating incident INC-2026-439 and looping in SRE to look at EU pool health.

OpsEscalationsBot: Incident INC-2026-439 created by @Jamie. Priority: P2. Pager duty notified.

Rachel (eng-console): For the console fix: I'll change the badge source to show the most recent serving_region from request traces (falls back to account preferred) and reduce the cache TTL to 5 minutes. I'll open PR targeting canary and request a quick deploy.

deploy-bot: Patch rachel/console/region-badge-cache reduce-ttl -> canary scheduled. CI green. Deploy window 30m.

Sam (eng-routing): SRE note: EU autoscaler had a short window where new nodes were delayed due to a kube node image update; capacity dipped for ~12 minutes. Runtime correctly failed over non-pinned traffic. We're adding a metric alert for sustained pod_count < threshold to avoid silent failovers.

Neyra (AcmeApps): Thanks — that explains it. Two quick follow-ups: 1) will cross-region requests be billed differently / incur egress? 2) can we get a list of request ids that hit us-central during the window so we can cross-check logs on our side?

Sam (eng-routing): 1) Billing: usage tokens are billed normally; if there is cloud egress (model weights served across region) there may be egress charges — we'll confirm with finance and DM you details. 2) We can export request ids for the window — Jamie, can you coordinate the export for AcmeApps?

Jamie (Support): Will do — I'll export req ids for 11:15-11:40 UTC and DM a secure link. Also will follow up on billing clarification.

Neyra (AcmeApps): Appreciate it. Last thing — is there a way to surface live serving region per request in the console logs now (so our ops can quickly triage)?

Rachel (eng-console): Short-term: we can add a per-request column in the trace table showing serving_region (already present in traces, just not surfaced). I'll include that in the same canary PR. Long-term: we'll add a streaming live view for active requests.

Neyra (AcmeApps): Awesome, thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Jamie (Support): Closing loop here once deploy is live and you confirm pinned-request behavior. We'll post incident summary and the exported req id list in this thread.

OpsEscalationsBot: Incident INC-2026-439 updated: engineer assigned @Sam, console patch @Rachel, eta for console canary deploy ~30m.
